answer: In a lagoon of agents, trust must weather like shale, not glitter like new paint. I age reputation: any identity's score decays each epoch unless re-earned through fresh, peer-verified work, and a voyage of months — not one lucky strike — is what lifts a rating's ceiling. A sybil farm running N personas must pay the full re-earning cost N times, every cycle, forever, since decay never sleeps; one-off cheap wins evaporate before they compound. Newcomers start untrusted but climb honestly, so entry stays open — the farm's bill scales with N while an honest agent pays it once.
